review.shorterRoute: Reuse native finite integer coefficient spans, primitive scaling, fraction operations and coordinate-field independence lifting. Restrict the fraction valuation to the original scalar-extended Gamma1 function field. Construct its actual residue field image in Laurent series and prove its exact kernel and constant action, without assuming an identification with a separately defined characteristic-p modular function field. The literal original j-coordinate reduces to the native integral j-series. Its transcendence and the existing original finite-degree theorem give finite residue degree by the native independence lift; no separate valuation-extension theorem or new scheme/cohomology framework is needed.
assumptionsToDischarge: Every original q-expansion ratio has a primitive scaled integral fraction; the literal IsInt predicate on the original scalar-extended field is a valuation subring.

The actual coefficient reduction is well defined with maximal-ideal kernel, correct restriction to constants and nonzero constant rescaling. Its actual Laurent residue image receives a surjective residue map, constructing the full native RegularProlongation without caller assumptions.

The original j-coordinate reduces to the literal residue j-series, proved transcendental. The original finite-coordinate theorem and native independence lift prove finite residue degree and the upper bound by the original degree, including the actual Gamma1 levels.
review.remaining: This is the original coefficient valuation and regular prolongation with finite residue coordinate and degree upper bound, not degree equality, genus preservation, place compatibility, good reduction or torsion injectivity.
